title: Infinity
examples: Can you explain what it means for a set to have infinite members?
Is infinity just a really big number, or is it something else?
How does Hilbert's hotel work with an infinite number of guests?

explain.say: Today we explore the idea of infinity in mathematics. It is a concept, not a regular number.

items: It is a concept of endlessness.
It is not a specific number.

draw.text: Infinity: A Concept, Not a Number

explain.say: We can compare the size of infinite sets. Some infinities are bigger than others.
Consider the set of whole numbers. If you remove some, the set is still infinite.
Hilbert's hotel shows how infinite sets behave with guests. It has infinitely many rooms.
If one new guest arrives, the hotel can always make space. They move everyone over.

items: Step 1: Move guest from Room N to Room N+1
End: Room 1 is now free for the new guest

explain.say: In real life, think about the number of seconds in a year. It is a very large, but finite, number.

faq.q: Is infinity the same as a really big number?
faq.a: No, infinity is a concept representing endlessness, not a number you can count to. It describes something without end.
asks: Is infinity just a very large number?

faq.q: How does Hilbert's hotel actually work?
faq.a: It shows that even if all rooms are full, you can always shift everyone to make space for one more person. This is due to the nature of infinity.
asks: Can you explain the hotel example?
If it's full, how do you add one more?

faq.q: Are all infinities the same size?
faq.a: No, mathematicians have shown that some infinite sets are much larger than others. This is a complex idea.
asks: Are there different sizes of infinity?
What makes one infinity bigger than another?

faq.q: Can I use infinity in everyday math problems?
faq.a: Usually, no. In practical math, we deal with finite numbers. Infinity helps us understand theoretical limits.
asks: Do I ever use infinity in school?
Is it useful for everyday calculations?

faq.q: What is the difference between countable and uncountable infinity?
faq.a: Countable means you can list the items one by one, like whole numbers. Uncountable means there are too many to list, like all points on a line.
asks: How do I know if a set is uncountable?

facts: Infinity is a concept describing endless quantity.
The set of natural numbers is considered a countably infinite set.
Hilbert's hotel is a thought experiment demonstrating properties of infinite sets.
The set of real numbers is an example of an uncountably infinite set.

quiz.say: If you have all the whole numbers, and you remove all the odd numbers, what is the remaining set?
quiz.why: Because the even numbers are still an infinite sequence, the resulting set is still infinite.

wrong.1: This is wrong because removing only the odd numbers leaves infinitely many even numbers.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the sequence of even numbers continues forever.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the set contains many numbers, not just one.

quiz.say: In Hilbert's hotel, if a new guest arrives, what is the easiest way to make room?

options.show: Move every current guest from Room N to Room N plus one
options.say: Move every current guest from Room N to Room N plus one

quiz.why: This process always frees up Room One, making space for the new arrival.

wrong.1: The hotel is assumed to have infinite rooms, so building is not the mathematical solution.
wrong.2: This assumes the guest has nowhere else to go, ignoring the infinite nature of the set.
wrong.3: Because the set is infinite, waiting for a departure might never happen.

quiz.say: Which type of infinity is represented by all the points on a line segment?
quiz.why: The points on a line are so numerous that you cannot list them one by one, making them uncountable.

wrong.0: This is wrong because countable sets can be put into a one-to-one correspondence with the natural numbers.
wrong.1: This is wrong because a line segment contains an endless amount of points.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the line segment has a measurable, non-zero length.
